Pairwise distances between distinct TALE domains

Source: R/distalr.R
tales_domain_distances.Rd

Step 2 of tales_compare(). Aligns every distinct domain sequence against every other and returns their pairwise dissimilarity.

Usage

tales_domain_distances(
  x,
  aln_method = "DECIPHER",
  ncores = 1,
  conda_bin = "auto"
)

Arguments

x

A tales object carrying dom_code, as returned by tales_assign_domain_codes().

aln_method

One of "DECIPHER" (the default), "Biostrings" or "mmseq2". "mmseq2" runs in the conda environment.

ncores

Number of cores for the pairwise alignment.

conda_bin

Passed to reticulate, for aln_method = "mmseq2".

Value

A domain_distances object, stamped with x's namespace.

Details

This is the expensive step, and the one worth having on its own: the repeat-level distances answer questions about repeat diversity that need no TALE-level alignment at all, and computing them does not require running ARLEM.

Distances are between distinct domains, keyed by dom_code, so the cost goes with the number of distinct sequences rather than the number of parts. See summary() for that ratio on a given object.

See also

tales_tale_distances(), which consumes this.

Other pairwise distances: as.matrix.pairwise_distances(), distances_assert_square(), distances_restrict(), is_pairwise_distances(), pairwise_distances(), tales_assign_domain_codes(), tales_compare(), tales_group(), tales_tale_distances(), validate_pairwise_distances()

Examples

x <- tales_from_telltale(system.file("extdata", "tellTaleExampleOutput",
                                     package = "tantale"))
xa <- tales_assign_domain_codes(x)
tales_domain_distances(xa)
#> Computing a distance matrix between TALE parts amino acid sequences using:
#> DECIPHER
